title: Ordered subset products in the trivial internal Koszul complex
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ be discrete, with trivial action on $R$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Put $K=K_R(R;1)$ with the signs of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. For $q\geq0$ let $S_q=R[0][-q]$ be the single-term complex, and write $u_I:S_{|I|}\to K$ for the chain map equal to $1_R$ on the subset $I$ and zero on the other subsets. Give $K$ the chain pairing $\star$ of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison] for the coefficient algebra $B=R$ with trivial action; explicitly,
$$(x\star y)_J=\sum_{A\sqcup C=J,\ |A|=p}(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}x_Ay_C\quad(x\in K^p,\ y\in K^q).$$
Let $m_{p,q}:S_p\otimes_R S_q\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{p+q}$ be the standard shift-tensor comparison followed by regular multiplication, in the displayed factor order, with no symmetry of factors: in its only nonzero degree $p+q$ it is the multiplication $R\otimes_RR\to R$ with no sign. After localization it is the derived identification $R[-p]\otimes^{\mathrm L}_RR[-q]\cong R[-p-q]$ that first removes the shift of the first factor and then that of the second, followed by the unitor.

The differential of $K$ is zero, and the subset inclusions give its canonical complex identification with $\bigoplus_I S_{|I|}$. The complex $K$ is K-flat (tensoring it with an acyclic complex gives an acyclic total complex). For all subsets $A,C$, as chain maps $S_{|A|}\otimes_R S_{|C|}\to K$,
$$\star\circ(u_A\otimes u_C)=\begin{cases}(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}u_{A\cup C}\circ m_{|A|,|C|},&A\cap C=\varnothing,\\0,&A\cap C\ne\varnothing.\end{cases}$$
For every strictly increasing list $i_1<\cdots<i_q$, the iterated chain product of $u_{\{i_1\}},\ldots,u_{\{i_q\}}$, using these ordered tensor identifications, equals $u_{\{i_1,\ldots,i_q\}}$ with coefficient $+1$ and zero in all other subset components. The empty product is $u_\varnothing$. These equalities hold also after localization $Q$ as equalities of derived morphisms, with $Q(\star)$ representing the derived tensor pairing. For $r=0$ the complex is $R[0]$ and the empty inclusion is its identity. The zero ring is allowed; no characteristic or completeness assumption is used.

proof.text: Use the supplied Koszul differential coordinates. For the trivial regular action every generator acts by identity, so differentialEntry is zero. Extend this to all degrees using the complex shape and biproduct extensionality.

Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-trivial-subset-decomposition] to the vanishing differentials to obtain the canonical inclusions, decomposition, empty unit and normalized rank-zero inverse. K-flatness is the given cup comparison field, without a new specialization or existence choice.

Take the single-complex shift and unsigned tensor isomorphisms and the invertible localization comparisons from [lem-sfb-koszul-single-tensor-normalization]. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-subset-shuffle-binary] to the canonical inclusion and tensor coordinates to obtain the binary chain formula.

Induct on the length of an increasing Fin-indexed list. Split off the final element. Every element in the earlier image is smaller than it, giving disjointness and an empty inversion filter. The binary identity therefore has coefficient one. Cancel mul.inv with mul.hom and use cardinality transports and the equality of the full image with the earlier image union the final singleton. The zero case is the empty inclusion.

Prove by induction for every list (with no monotonicity hypothesis) that derivedOrderedProduct equals Q.map orderedProduct. The successor step uses tensorator naturality and cancellation of its specified inverse. Tensorator naturality, additivity of Q, and the binary chain formula give derived_binary in both the disjoint and intersecting cases. The chain increasing identity then gives derived_increasing. Assemble all fields of Products.

proof_origin.place: A3 Lean reduction: canonical subset decomposition, single-complex normalization and binary shuffle are separate argument steps. Zero differentials, increasing induction, K-flatness from cup and localization naturality are proved in the item.
